full_judgment: 15. In the decision of Md Lutfur Rahman vs State and another, reported in the same volume i.e. 4 BLT (AD) 244, the Appellate Division held that offence under section 376, Penal Code is not compoundable, as such, the case cannot be withdrawn. This view was further emphasized by the Appellate Division in the decision of Sorhesh Ali and another vs Jarina Begum and another, reported in 49 DLR (AD) 143 wherein it has been held that offence under section 376 of the Penal Code is not compoundable offence, as such, there is no question of withdrawal. The Appellate Division in the decision of Abdul Khaleque and others vs Md Hanif and others, reported in 49 DLR (AD) 134, was of the opinion that for filing an application under section 494 of the Code of Criminal Procedure two conditions must be fulfilled i.e. the application must be filed by the public prosecutor on behalf of the State and Court is to accord consent. The Court held that section 494 of the Code of Criminal Procedure gives the authority only to a public prosecutor to file an application for withdrawal, not to the accused persons.
